title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: generative AI apps indicators as triggers in Risky AI usage policies
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned triggers from today's documented controls and reports the stale roadmap target as a target. Minor corrections should clarify the app-selection route, narrow the policy-creation row, acknowledge differing trigger documentation and name the published billing meter.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support generative AI apps indicators as triggers in Risky AI usage policies.
claims.quote: With this update, the generative AI apps indicators will be supported as triggers in Risky AI usage policy.

claims.claim: Triggers define the conditions that bring a user into policy scope.
claims.quote: With triggers, customers can define the conditions for bringing the user into the scope of a policy

claims.claim: The generative AI apps indicators determine the risk score.
claims.quote: while the generative AI apps indicators are used to determine risk score.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe setup of generative AI apps indicators as Risky AI usage triggers.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management 501538 triggers; generative AI apps triggers Risky AI usage default existing policies. Opened policy templates, policy indicators and configure; Risky AI usage has a blank triggers cell and no setup steps.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sources do not state what these new triggers do on arrival or whether existing Risky AI usage policies change.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management generative AI apps triggers Risky AI usage default existing policies. Read roadmap, templates, indicators and configure; none states the new triggers' arrival default or changes to existing policies.

claims.claim: Triggering events are prerequisites that determine whether a user is active for a policy.
claims.quote: Triggering events are prerequisites that determine if a user is active for an Insider Risk Management policy.

claims.claim: A user without a triggering event is not evaluated unless manually added in the Users dashboard.
claims.quote: If you add a user to an Insider Risk Management policy but the user doesn't have a triggering event, the policy doesn't evaluate the user's activity unless you manually add the user in the Users dashboard.

claims.claim: Policy indicators determine a risk score once a user is in scope.
claims.quote: Indicators included in Insider Risk Management policies determine a risk score for an in-scope user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Generative AI apps indicators analyse prompts and responses to detect risky interactions or sharing of confidential information.
claims.quote: Use these indicators in policies to analyze interactions (prompts and responses) entered into these applications and help detect inappropriate or risky interactions or sharing of confidential information.

claims.claim: The generative AI apps indicators section lists Microsoft Copilot experiences, Enterprise AI apps, Other AI applications and Azure AI Content Safety indicators.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot experiences; Enterprise AI apps; Other AI applications; Azure AI Content Safety indicators

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The indicator settings page says triggering events are customisable only for Data leaks and Data leaks by priority users, not Risky AI usage.
claims.quote: You can only modify triggering events for policies created from the Data leaks or Data leaks by priority users templates. Policies created from all other templates don't have customizable triggering indicators or events.
claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the indicator settings page, then add: 'The Get started workflow also documents Communication Compliance and HR trigger options for Data leaks by risky users and Security policy violations by risky users; it still gives no Risky AI usage trigger setup.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management requires a supported Microsoft 365 subscription and appropriate user licences.
claims.quote: To access and use Insider Risk Management, administrators need to verify their organization has a supported subscription and assign the appropriate licenses to users.

claims.claim: The licensing model combines subscription entitlement with pay-as-you-go indicators.
claims.quote: This feature uses pay-as-you-go billing or per-user licensing for Microsoft Purview capabilities or both.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot experiences indicator requires pay-as-you-go billing for non-Microsoft 365 AI data.
claims.quote: To use the Microsoft Copilot experiences indicator for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: The Enterprise AI apps indicator requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: To use the Enterprise AI apps indicator, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: The Other AI applications indicator requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Other AI applications: AI applications that users in your organization discover from their browser activity. ... To use this indicator, enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: Detecting risky interactions for Microsoft 365 Copilot data has no pay-as-you-go requirement or charge.
claims.quote: There aren't any pay-as-you-go billing requirements or charges for Microsoft 365 detecting inappropriate or risky interaction for Microsoft 365 Copilot data.

claims.quote: Searched: generative AI apps indicators PowerShell API; Insider Risk Management policy indicators configure PowerShell New-InsiderRiskPolicy Set-InsiderRiskPolicy Microsoft Graph API. Read indicator settings and configure; results give portal controls, not a setting operation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management > Policies > Create policy opens the policy workflow in Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Go to the Insider Risk Management solution. ... Select Policies in the left navigation. ... Select Create policy to open the policy workflow.
claims.fix: Keep the documented path and narrow the row's governs text to 'Opening the Insider Risk Management policy creation workflow'. Create policy opens creation, not editing, and the row already states that Risky AI usage trigger setup is undocumented.

claims.claim: Learn documents no PowerShell or API operation for creating or editing Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Insider Risk Management policy PowerShell cmdlet; policy indicators configure PowerShell New-InsiderRiskPolicy Set-InsiderRiskPolicy Microsoft Graph API. Opened configure and policies; results document portal workflows and case/user automation, not policy CRUD.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users is the route to role-group membership.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups ... Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the role group through Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... -Identity ... Applicable: ... Security & Compliance ... -Member ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)
